name: Black Butte Ranch
label: Black Butte Ranch
about_prose: Black Butte Ranch sits eight miles northwest of Sisters, Oregon, on 1,800 acres at 3,376 feet in the eastern Cascade foothills, bordered on several sides by Deschutes National Forest. Black Butte, the 6,436-foot cinder cone the ranch takes its name from, rises just to the northeast. The land was cattle range before it was a resort. Stewart Lowery, a San Francisco businessman, bought the property in the mid-1930s and gave it the Black Butte Ranch name. Howard Morgan, a former Oregon Public Utility Commissioner, owned it through the 1960s, then sold it in 1969 to Brooks Resources Corporation, a Central Oregon timber company branching into recreational development. Brooks took full title in January 1970 and started building. It was the company's first project in the region.

The first homeowners moved in during 1971, the same year the ranch got its own post office. Brooks Resources ran the development through the 1970s, then handed the roads, bike paths, and common areas to the homeowners association in 1982. Five years later, in 1987, the association bought the two golf courses and the Lodge outright, and it has owned and operated the whole resort since. Brooks also shaped the town of Sisters at the same time, offering local merchants free architectural help and no-interest loans in the 1970s to adopt the Western storefront look that still defines Sisters' downtown today. Of the 1,251 homesites platted across the ranch, about 20 remain undeveloped.

What the ranch offers is room to move. Two 18-hole courses anchor it. Big Meadow was designed by Robert Muir Graves, and Glaze Meadow was redesigned by John Fought in 2012. The 12-hole Little Meadow putting course rounds out the golf. Aspen Lake and Phalarope Lake sit inside the property line, both reachable by bike path, with a nature trail running along Phalarope Lake to Big Meadow. Twenty-seven miles of paved path connect the neighborhoods to five pools, 14 tennis courts, and 12 pickleball courts. Wranglers lead horseback rides through the meadows, and there is disc golf on the grounds too. The Lodge itself is new. The ranch tore down the original 50-year-old lodge and replaced it with a 22,100-square-foot building that opened in May 2023, clad in charred cedar siding with a Douglas fir and slate interior and a stone fireplace built to echo the region's volcanic rock formations. The Lodge Restaurant and the Lakeside Bistro inside it are open to non-owners. Homes range from Lodge-area condos to custom builds on the golf courses, and owners can enroll a property in the ranch's own nightly rental program for the weeks they are not using it themselves.

Full-time residents are the exception here, not the rule. The 2020 Census counted 260 year-round residents on the ranch, down from 366 in 2010. The peak season population, owners, renters, and day guests combined, runs close to 5,000. Families who do live here year-round send their kids to Sisters School District 6, the same district that serves the town of Sisters eight miles away. That is worth confirming directly if you are comparing school ratings online. A separate district, the Black Butte School District, is a small K-8 system near Camp Sherman that covers a different Black Butte entirely and is easy to confuse with the ranch by name alone.

The same forest border that gives the ranch its privacy is also its exposure. Wildfire has reached the property more than once. The Cache Mountain Fire in 2002 destroyed two homes and threatened roughly 80 more before crews stopped it. The B&B Complex fires in 2003 and the GW Fire in 2007 also came close enough to matter. It is also a real drive from anywhere else, 45 minutes to Bend and about 30 to Redmond Municipal Airport, so daily errands take planning that a Bend neighborhood does not require. And the neighborhood empties out for long stretches between ski season and summer. Anyone weighing a full-time move here should plan around that quiet, not against it.

amenities.name: Big Meadow Golf Course
amenities.description: An 18-hole course designed by Robert Muir Graves, playing over 7,000 yards from the championship tees, with Cascade views.

amenities.name: Glaze Meadow Golf Course
amenities.description: An 18-hole course playing 7,007 yards from the back tees, renovated in 2012 by John Fought, with five tee sets and grass-faced bunkers.

amenities.name: Little Meadow Putting Course
amenities.description: A 12-hole putting course by John Fought, with holes between 45 and 105 feet.

amenities.name: The Lodge Restaurant
amenities.description: The main dining venue, with Pacific Northwest cuisine and mountain views, alongside the Aspen Lounge.

amenities.name: Lakeside Bistro
amenities.description: Casual lakeside dining with breakfast, pizza, and craft beers.

amenities.name: Trails and Bike Paths
amenities.description: 27 miles of paved paths for biking, walking, and winter Nordic skiing, plus a private lake for fly fishing, canoeing, and paddleboarding.

amenities.name: Black Butte Ranch Spa
amenities.description: Full-service spa with massage, facial, and body treatments, with online booking.

membership_tiers.label: 7-day full
membership_tiers.name: 7-day full golf annual pass
membership_tiers.description: Black Butte Ranch sells season passes for Big Meadow and Glaze Meadow rather than a club membership with an initiation fee. Play any day. Passholders get 20 percent off in the golf shops. The 2026 passes run through March 31, 2027.

membership_tiers.label: 5-day weekday
membership_tiers.name: 5-day weekday golf annual pass
membership_tiers.description: Weekday play only, Monday through Friday, excluding May 27 and September 2.

membership_tiers.label: 7-day afternoon
membership_tiers.name: 7-day afternoon golf annual pass
membership_tiers.description: Any day of the week, tee times after 1pm.

membership_tiers.label: Cart
membership_tiers.name: Golf cart annual pass
membership_tiers.description: Unlimited cart use for the season at half the rider price.

course_specs.summary: Two 18-hole championship courses: Big Meadow (Robert Muir Graves, 7,000+ yds) and Glaze Meadow (John Fought renovation 2012, 7,007 yds), plus the 12-hole Little Meadow putting course.

sources.supports: Read from the raw page HTML, not a summary. The Golf Annual Pass table lists, verbatim, "7-DAY FULL ANNUAL PASS 7 Days Anytime", "7-DAY AFTERNOON ANNUAL PASS After 1pm", "5 1/2-DAY ANNUAL PASS Sun Noon - Fri", "5-DAY WEEKDAY PASS Mon-Fri Excludes 5/27 & 9/2" and "4 1/2-DAY GOLF PASS Sun 12pm-Thurs", with an INDIVIDUAL row of $2,775, $1,525, $2,475, $2,275, $1,875 and a 2ND FAMILY MEMBER row of $2,325, blank, $2,175, $1,975, $1,575, plus "GOLF CART ANNUAL PASS 1/2 rider price Unlimited use $560". Also verbatim: "Passes are valid through 3/31/27" and "All Passholders receive a 20% discount at Black Butte Ranch Golf Shops." The page's own early-payment discount, "$50 discount if paid by 3/31/26", has expired and is deliberately not published here. Only the 7-day full, 5-day weekday, 7-day afternoon and cart passes are carried into membership_tiers. These passes are optional. Black Butte Ranch's mandatory association assessment is NOT published anywhere reachable: blackbutteranchhoa.com serves a login form and nothing else, and the association's own recorded Rules and Regulations reference "dues and Assessments" without stating an amount.
Drive times consistent with the existing drive_times field: 45 minutes to Bend, about 30 minutes to Redmond Municipal Airport.
